The change is in `src/click/types.py:261` (`Choice.get_metavar`):

- When the parameter is an option with `show_choices=False`, the metavar is built from the choices' inferred param-type names (`convert_type(type(choice)).name.upper()`), de-duplicated in first-seen order via `dict.fromkeys` and joined with `|` — so `["foo", "bar"] → [TEXT]`, `[1, 2] → [INTEGER]`, `["foo", 1] → [TEXT|INTEGER]`.
- Every other case (options with the default `show_choices=True`, and arguments, including the required-argument `{...}` form) still joins the choice values as before.

`python -m pytest -q -o pythonpath=src tests/test_options.py` → 113 passed.

argv:
Bug report for this repository (click):

An option declared with `type=click.Choice([...])` and `show_choices=False` still shows the
choice values in the `--help` metavar, e.g. `-g [foo|bar]`. With `show_choices=False` the
metavar should show the *type names* of the choices instead — the `name` of the param type each
choice value converts to, upper-cased, de-duplicated in first-seen order, joined with `|`:
`[TEXT]` for string choices, `[INTEGER]` for ints, `[FLOAT]`, `[BOOLEAN]`, and `[TEXT|INTEGER]`
for `["foo", 1]`. Options with `show_choices=True` (the default) and arguments keep showing the
values.

Change as little as possible and do not edit the tests. The test command is
`python -m pytest -q -o pythonpath=src tests/test_options.py`; run it once at the end.
